name: Fix role-based access check on privileged admin action
query: Our plugin's cache-purge handler registered on admin_post_purge_cache is supposed to be limited to administrators, but we gated it with `if ( in_array( 'administrator', wp_get_current_user()->roles, true ) )`. Customers on multisite installs that use custom admin roles report they cannot run the action. Fix the check so it grants access correctly.
expected_behavior: Identify that the handler gates access by testing role membership via wp_get_current_user()->roles instead of verifying a capability

Replace the in_array() role test with current_user_can( 'manage_options' ), the capability the skill prescribes for site-level operations, so custom roles and multisite super admins granted the capability pass
Pair the capability check with nonce verification using check_admin_referer( 'purge_cache' ) at the start of the handler
Branch on the result of current_user_can() and fail closed with wp_die( ..., 403 ) when the check fails, so the check is never called and ignored
Keep the guard inside the admin_post handler itself, since the admin-post.php URL is directly reachable and hiding the button or menu entry is not security
Run any request input through wp_unslash() and sanitize/validate it (e.g. absint()) before use in privileged work
Avoid any code path that reads or assigns roles from the request; authorization must rest solely on the capability check
success_criteria: The handler authorizes with current_user_can() using a capability such as manage_options, and no role-membership test (in_array over wp_get_current_user()->roles) remains
The capability check branches on its result and fails closed with a 403 wp_die() before purge_cache() or any privileged work runs
Nonce verification with check_admin_referer() is present before the capability check on this state-changing action
Users granted the capability via custom roles or multisite promotion can run the action, while subscribers and authors without it cannot
The guard executes in the handler itself, not only where the button or menu item is rendered
